title: Unpolled stdout/stderr can block child completion
behavior: stdout_task and stderr_task are local async futures, not spawned tasks. The code pins them but awaits only status_fut until the child is reaped, then starts join! on the pipe readers under a grace timeout.
technical_explanation: Pinning does not poll a future. A child that fills either OS pipe blocks on write while the parent waits for exit; without a deadline/cancellation that can wait indefinitely. With a timeout it can be killed even though it would complete if output were drained. Streaming callbacks also do not run during the pending normal child wait.
parity_relation: Overlaps AGENT-050 shell execution/streaming parity and is an independent correctness defect in process I/O.
assumptions: Requires enough output to fill a pipe while the process is running. OS pipe capacity is platform-dependent; no fixed threshold is claimed. Timeout/cancellation depends on supplied options.

title: Failed UI queue admission does not recover the cleared prompt draft
behavior: A failed busy steering/follow-up request restores pending images but leaves the submitted text absent from the editor and queue. The follow-up path also clears the draft before idle admission and can lose it when the run-slot reservation fails.
technical_explanation: Editor::submit stores expanded text in its own history, clears undo/redo, calls a callback with no acceptance result, and clears unconditionally. The busy callback spawns lane.steer and restores only images on Err. Follow-up bypasses submit, clears first, then either reserves the idle slot or spawns lane.follow_up; its error branch also restores only images. A failed try_start_working has no recovery branch, and the idle channel-send result is discarded. The normal native Up/Down handler uses a separate TuiState history, so the Editor-internal history does not establish normal UI recovery of the busy submission.

The source contains an internal Editor history copy for ordinary Enter, so permanent loss from all memory is not asserted. No interactive run or failing queue request was executed.

title: Renamed session-value discriminator omits historical native values during restoration
behavior: When a historical native session still contains customType='ice.value' records and no external migration has rewritten them before loading, active SessionValues omits those records from its latest-wins value view. The underlying generic custom entries can remain in the session log. A concrete native caller loads display.hide_thinking through this API; under that condition, an older saved session preference is not restored and the existing settings default remains.
technical_explanation: The local identity change replaces VALUE_CUSTOM_TYPE='ice.value' with 'icers.value' at values.rs:32. SessionValues::load passes the new discriminator into an exact custom_type storage query at lines 43-53; from_entries also skips every entry whose custom_type differs from that constant at lines 57-82. SessionValueWriter appends only the new discriminator at lines 119-147. A complete active crates search for ice.value, icers.value and VALUE_CUSTOM_TYPE found only the new constant/example, its two read filters, its writer and the module re-export. Both production direct callers found by the scoped caller search pass harness.session() directly to load. In the bounded native JSONL path, the custom-entry decoder copies the raw customType string, replay changes parent_id rather than the discriminator, and common query matching compares custom_type exactly. No historical alias or rewrite appears in that inspected path.
assumptions: Requires historical raw native ice.value records to reach the active API without an external migration. This is source-level reasoning, not a reproduced runtime result. No real sessions or user configuration directories were inspected; no application, test, terminal or migration was executed. External import/migration utilities and arbitrary third-party SessionStorage implementations were not exhaustively inspected. This finding concerns values omitted from the projected view, not deletion of the generic log records.

The inspected TypeScript gap entries do not establish a precise existing SESSION owner for the generic native SessionValues API, so entry_ids is intentionally empty. The existing native read/write API and the remaining v4 durability behavior stay credited.
